case_title: Mahesh Kumar v. State of Haryana
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (the accused was the victim's husband)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B; Evidence Act s.113-B (presumption, considered)
weapon: Poison (organophosphorus pesticide, as alleged by the State)
evidence_type: Oral testimony (father PW3 and brother PW4); documentary (letters Ex.PF/1, Ex.PK/1, Ex.PG/1; memorandum Ex.PE/1); investigation records
mitigating_circumstances: Protracted trial of more than 15 years (noted by High Court when reducing sentence)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.304-B IPC; sentence of ten years
high_court_outcome: Conviction affirmed; sentence reduced from ten years to seven years (co-accused mother-in-law acquitted on appeal)
neutral_facts: The victim married the accused in May 1991. The victim's father alleged that after the marriage the victim was mistreated by her husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law and sister-in-law because they demanded dowry. The father said he gave dowry beyond his means, gave a gold chain about a year after the marriage, and paid cash sums on later occasions, but the in-laws continued to demand money and beat the victim. The victim had written letters about the harassment. In February 1994 the victim's father was informed that the victim had died in hospital, and he alleged that the in-laws had administered poison. A first information report was lodged the next day against four family members, who were arrested. The prosecution relied on the oral statements of the victim's father and brother and on several letters written by the victim, including one to her father about the in-laws and the gold chain, one to a brother-in-law saying her husband beat her daily, and one about her mother-in-law's dislike of her cooking. A written memorandum dated January 1992, said to record a settlement executed by the in-laws before panchayat members, was also relied upon, though no panchayat member was examined. The death was attributed to organophosphorus pesticide poisoning.
offence_severity: Minimum 7 years; maximum imprisonment for life
physical_harm: Death of the victim in hospital on or about 08.02.1994, alleged to be caused by poison
financial_property_loss: Alleged dowry payments: gold chain and Rs.1,000 and Rs.2,000 in cash; alleged further demand of Rs.5,000 (allegations only, not court findings)
motive: alleged: demand for dowry by the in-laws; the Supreme Court held this demand was not proved
key_evidence_accepted: No evidence accepted as proving a dowry demand or soon-before cruelty; the Court found the oral statements of PW3 and PW4 insufficient and the letters did not support the prosecution
witness_credibility: Statements of PW3 (father) and PW4 (brother) held insufficient without independent evidence, which was available but not examined; no express finding of dishonesty
bail_history: Not stated during trial; bail bonds discharged on acquittal
trial_duration: offence: not given (death reported 08.02.1994); trial judgment: 12.12.1995; High Court: 21.01.2009; Supreme Court: 07.08.2019
legal_representation: Appellant: D. N. Goburdhan, Adv. State: Shekhar Raj Sharma and Vishwa Pal Singh, Advs.
investigation_status: FIR lodged 09.02.1994; investigation completed by IO Assim Khan; all four accused arrested; charge sheet filed and case committed to trial court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.304-B, ten years. High Court: conviction affirmed, sentence reduced to seven years. Supreme Court: conviction set aside and accused acquitted
prosecution_argument: The victim died within seven years of marriage by unnatural death (organophosphorus pesticide), and the evidence showed continuous cruelty over dowry
defence_argument: Essential ingredients of s.304-B not proved; letters do not relate to dowry demand; the gold chain demand was too remote to be soon before death; no evidence of demand soon before death
legal_principle_applied: Section 304-B requires proof of dowry-related cruelty or harassment soon before death, with a proximate nexus to death; the s.113-B presumption arises only after this initial proof
precedent_relied_upon: Satvir Singh v. State of Punjab (2001) 8 SCC 633; Hira Lal v. State (Govt. of NCT), Delhi (2003) 8 SCC 80; Sakatar Singh v. State of Haryana (2004) 11 SCC 291; Major Singh v. State of Punjab (2015) 5 SCC 201
other_sentence_order: Conviction set aside; accused set at liberty unless involved in another case; bail bonds discharged
